title: What The Kora Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal West African philosophy absurdist
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The kora is a twenty-one string harp-lute situation
Built from a calabash and goatskin — remarkable creation
The griots of West Africa have played this thing for years
Carrying history in notes because they couldn't use arrears

[Pre-Chorus]
I watched a man play kora in a documentary once
The way his thumbs moved — I felt immediately a dunce

[Chorus]
What does the kora know that I don't know?
It knows the whole genealogy three hundred years ago
What does the kora know in the evening air?
It knows the names of every king before the kings were there
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The griot is the keeper of the oral history
The kora is the vessel and the melody's the key
Twenty-one strings tuned to a pentatonic framework
Playing memory so accurate it functions like a network

[Bridge]
You come from somewhere — the kora can prove this
Your family's in the music and the music's in the roots, miss
I come from Scotland and Zimbabwe and Perth, Western Australia
The kora just added that up and filed it — pure regalia

[Outro]
Kora knows… the whole story… kora knows
That's my boy
